intro.en: English is limited outside hotels, but goodwill is not. These six carry most of a trip — and the local dialect, Hakata-ben, is softer and friendlier than textbook Japanese.

text.en: Excuse me / sorry / may I have your attention. The single most useful word in Japan; say it before everything else.
"This one, please" — point at the menu, the display case or the plastic food model. Nobody minds pointing.
"Extra noodles, please", for when your ramen bowl still has broth in it. A local move, and always well received.

meta.en: おすすめはなんですか

text.en: "What do you recommend?" At a yatai or a small izakaya this is the best order you can make.
"Thank you for the meal", said on the way out. It lands warmly, especially with an older cook.
Hakata dialect for "it's fine" and "no need". You will hear them constantly; using one gets you a smile.
